findings.reason: the investigation's central decision is path identity versus a live-claim check, and a worker told that the run-id resolver also names by session and node will scope the rename to `_launch_worktree_path` alone and leave gc's per-run sweep resolving a path that no longer exists.
findings.text: §3 says "A worktree path is derived from the session and node id (`_launch_worktree_path` near line 2134, `_run_worktree_path` near line 1206), not the run id", but `_run_worktree_path` derives nothing from ids: it iterates `list_live()` and the project's ledger rows matching `run_id` and returns the `worktree` value they carry (routing.py:1217–1234), and it is the resolver gc.py:481 uses to confine a run's sweep — so it is the one consumer that already resolves a tree by run identity, and the repair's "path identity" option must keep it coherent.

findings.reason: extracting lines 837–879 alone reproduces the class of divergence the section is written to remove, and the fix belongs in the plan as a stated preparation step the extracted function owes or the queue path must perform.
findings.text: §2 states the extracted function returns "the node-contract verdict a single dispatch reaches", but two of the checks read fields that plan_dispatch fills in immediately before them and the queue path does not: `assess_execution_fit` and `gate_population_finding` judge `node.done_when` as extended by `with_carried_findings` (dispatch_plan.py:809–819, the only call site in the tree), and `negative_control_finding` judges `node.write_paths` after the run-directory default is applied (dispatch_plan.py:830–833) — so a batch entry can pass at queue time and be refused at launch, which is the defect the node exists to close.
